issues.legal_issue: A public development authority may not dispose of land reserved for planned future development through an opaque bulk sale that departs from its public-service purposes and lacks adequate approval and competition.
material_facts: The authority held undeveloped land that had been left for future planning as the township developed and its needs changed.
It moved quickly to sell large plots to private developers, rather than continue planned development for the township’s residents.
The sales proceeded without a reasoned decision by the authority’s board, at prices below the stated reserve price, and without an open competitive process that gave others a fair opportunity to bid.
The authority’s purposes included planned development, affordable housing and provision for community and environmental needs.
issues.conclusion: The impugned bulk sales were vitiated and could not bind the authority; the High Court’s disapproval of bulk sale was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: A public body entrusted with land for planned development must act transparently and for public good, not merely to make money. Bulk sale was contrary to the authority’s objectives in the circumstances. Even if a sale of remaining land were necessary, it required a well-considered decision at the highest level and sale by public auction or tenders after wider publicity. The Court relied on Article 226’s public-law review of public bodies and the authority’s statutory planning role under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966; no earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

rule.if: public_development_authority and land_reserved_for_future_planning and bulk_sale_to_private_developers and (sale_lacked_reasoned_high_level_approval or sale_lacked_open_competition)

predicates.public_development_authority: A public body was entrusted with land to carry out development for the public.
predicates.land_reserved_for_future_planning: Land was left undeveloped so its future use could be planned in light of later development and community needs.
predicates.bulk_sale_to_private_developers: The authority proposed or made a bulk sale of the land to private developers.
predicates.sale_lacked_reasoned_high_level_approval: The bulk sale was not supported by a reasoned decision at the authority’s highest or competent level.
predicates.sale_lacked_open_competition: The sale did not provide an adequately public and competitive opportunity for others to bid.

issues.definition: When a public development authority bulk-sells land reserved for future planning without reasoned high-level approval or open competition, the bulk sale is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Land reserved for future development may not be allotted for development before the required development plan has been approved.
material_facts: The land was left as developable land pending a later plan for its use.
The revised development plan concerning the allotments had not been approved by the State Government when the allotments were made.
The allotments specified uncertain or insufficiently established uses for parts of the land.
issues.conclusion: The allotments made before approval of the required development plan were invalid; land reverting to the authority must be used in accordance with the plan sanctioned by the State Government.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 115 and 43 of the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, development and land use are governed by the statutory planning process and applicable restrictions. The Court upheld the conclusion that the relevant draft development plan had not received the approval required by section 115 and directed that returned land be used strictly in accordance with the sanctioned plan. No earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

predicates.planning_authority_disposal: A planning authority allotted or disposed of land under its control.
predicates.land_use_plan_unapproved: The plan governing the land’s proposed use had not received the required governmental approval.
predicates.allotment_depends_on_unapproved_plan: The allotment relied on a proposed use that depended on the unapproved plan.

issues.definition: When a planning authority makes an allotment that depends on a land-use plan which has not received required approval, the allotment is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A public office-holder’s direct or indirect connection to entities seeking public land requires disclosure and separation from dealings with the public body.
material_facts: A person who held a directorship in the public development authority was connected with entities that sought and obtained allotments of authority land.
Those entities included family members and close relations, and the authority was not specifically informed of the connections when dealing with them.
The allotments were made through a process that lacked transparency and adequate competitive safeguards.
issues.conclusion: The transactions were vitiated; the office-holder’s indirect involvement did not cease to matter merely because the office-holder was not formally part of the allotment decisions.
issues.legal_principle: Public office is held in trust for public good and requires probity. An office-holder who proposes to deal with the public body, directly or indirectly, should not hold that office; alternatively, the office-holder must clearly disclose the connection so the body can deal with the applicant with full awareness. The Court applied public-law principles of transparency and proper conduct; no earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

rule.if: public_office_holder_involved_in_public_land_decisions and connected_entities_sought_public_land and connection_not_disclosed and allotment_process_lacked_transparency

predicates.public_office_holder_involved_in_public_: A person holding public office participated in or had access to the public body’s land-related affairs.
predicates.connected_entities_sought_public_land: Entities connected to that office-holder sought or obtained land from the public body.
predicates.connection_not_disclosed: The office-holder did not clearly disclose the connection to the public body before it dealt with the entities.
predicates.allotment_process_lacked_transparency: The allotment process did not transparently safeguard the public body’s interests.

issues.definition: When connected entities seek public land, the connection is undisclosed, and the allotment process lacks transparency, an allotment associated with a public office-holder’s involvement is vitiated.

issues.legal_issue: A public-interest challenge may proceed when the petitioner’s earlier dealings with the public body do not establish participation in or competition over the challenged transactions.
material_facts: The petitioner was not shown to have participated in the challenged land transactions or competed with the successful allottees for those allotments.
The petitioner had obtained other land from the authority in the past, but that fact did not establish that the petitioner was a business rival in the challenged transactions.
The High Court independently framed broader public-interest issues and examined the authority’s conduct.
issues.conclusion: The objection that the petition was an individual business grievance was rejected, and the public-interest proceedings were properly entertained.
issues.legal_principle: A prior allotment from a public body does not, by itself, establish that a petitioner is a competitor in later transactions or defeat public-interest review. In Article 226 public-interest proceedings, the court may examine public injury, public duty and the conduct of a public body beyond the petitioner’s individual allegations. No earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

rule.if: public_interest_proceeding and petitioner_not_participant_in_challenged_transaction and prior_public_allotment_only and court_examined_broader_public_interest

predicates.public_interest_proceeding: The proceeding was brought or taken up to examine an alleged injury to the public interest.
predicates.petitioner_not_participant_in_challenged: The petitioner did not participate in or bid against the successful applicants in the challenged transaction.
predicates.prior_public_allotment_only: The asserted basis for alleged rivalry was that the petitioner had obtained a different allotment from the public body at another time.
predicates.court_examined_broader_public_interest: The court framed or considered issues extending beyond the petitioner’s individual grievance.

issues.definition: When a petitioner did not participate in the challenged transaction and the alleged rivalry rests only on an earlier allotment, broader public-interest review may proceed.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot successfully object to a lack of pleadings or opportunity when the court identified the issues for consideration and allowed the parties a full opportunity to respond.
material_facts: The High Court framed questions identifying the matters it intended to examine, including the propriety of bulk sale, public interest, procedural irregularities and pricing.
The parties were put on notice of those issues and were allowed to submit pleadings and documents in their defence.
The court examined the authority’s records and based its findings on the recorded facts and inferences from them.
issues.conclusion: The appellants could not complain that the High Court lacked necessary pleadings or denied them an opportunity to defend themselves.
issues.legal_principle: In public-interest jurisdiction under Article 226, technical pleading requirements do not prevent a constitutional court from examining public injury and enforcing public duty where affected parties have notice of the issues and a full opportunity to respond. No earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

predicates.public_interest_proceeding: The court was conducting a public-interest proceeding concerning a public body’s conduct.
predicates.court_identified_issues_in_advance: The court stated the issues it proposed to examine before deciding them.
predicates.parties_had_full_opportunity_to_respond: The parties had a full opportunity to present pleadings and evidence on the identified issues.

issues.definition: When a court identifies the issues in a public-interest proceeding and gives the parties a full opportunity to respond, an objection based on lack of pleadings or opportunity is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: Relief for an invalid public-land allotment may be tailored where substantial construction or third-party interests have made complete reversal impracticable.
material_facts: The allotments were held to be vitiated.
On one allotted plot, substantial residential construction had been completed and flats had been booked by members of the public.
For another allotment, the extent of construction and any third-party interests required inspection and demarcation.
For an allotment where no construction or third-party interests were shown, the Court sustained resumption of the land.
issues.conclusion: The allotment with substantial construction and third-party interests was not undone outright but was made subject to payment of the reserve price; land with substantial construction under another allotment was to be identified and retained only to the extent needed for practical use, with the undeveloped remainder reverting to the authority; land without such circumstances reverted to the authority.
issues.legal_principle: A change in the status quo during litigation is at the risk of those benefiting from it, but relief may be adjusted to avoid imposing the consequences of an invalid transaction on innocent third parties where the situation has become irreversible. The Court required payment of the proper price for retained land and resumption of land where no comparable irreversible interests existed. No earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

predicates.invalid_public_land_allotment: A public body’s allotment of land was found to be legally vitiated.
predicates.substantial_construction_completed: Substantial buildings had been constructed on the allotted land before final resolution of the dispute.
predicates.innocent_third_party_interests_created: People who were not responsible for the defective allotment had acquired interests in the resulting property.

issues.definition: When an invalid public-land allotment has led to substantial construction or innocent third-party interests, built land may be retained on fair payment while unbuilt land reverts.

issues.legal_issue: Leave to appeal may be refused where an earlier judgment has disposed of the proposed appellant’s claim and the proposed appellant does not disclose the membership of the society on whose behalf it proceeds.
material_facts: A proposed housing society challenged the cancellation of its allotment in a separate writ petition.
The High Court had dismissed that petition after deciding the broader public-interest proceeding on the same day.
The appeal was brought in the proposed society’s name through one member, but the membership of the proposed society was not disclosed and the writ petition filed below was not produced.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused leave to appeal and dismissed the petition.
issues.legal_principle: In exercising its special-leave jurisdiction under Article 136, the Court found no basis to grant leave where the prior judgment had disposed of the society’s claim and the proposed society had not disclosed its members or produced the underlying petition. No earlier case is identified in the supplied judgment as the basis for this holding.

predicates.special_leave_proceeding: A party sought permission to appeal to the Supreme Court.
predicates.earlier_judgment_disposed_of_claim: An earlier judgment had already disposed of the claim underlying the proposed appeal.
predicates.society_members_not_disclosed: A society seeking to appeal did not disclose who its members were.

issues.definition: When an earlier judgment has disposed of a claim and a society seeking special leave does not disclose its members, leave to appeal is denied.
